Tile type: {type}
Suitable for the selected tile role
Format: exactly {format}
Format: freely selectable length and width, e.g. 600 × 300 mm.
Format: square, e.g. 300 × 300 mm.
Format: freely selectable edge length, e.g. 150 mm.
Format: aspect ratio from {min}:1 to {max}:1, e.g. 600 × 100 mm.
Format: aspect ratio of at least {min}:1, e.g. 1,200 × 200 mm.
Format: length = {count} × width + {gaps} × joint; with a {joint} mm joint, e.g. {length} × 100 mm.

Multiple herringbone: length ≥ {count} × width + {gaps} × joint; with a {joint} mm joint, e.g. at least {length} × 100 mm. The tile bundle may remain rectangular and does not have to close as a square.
Frame format: length > width + joint. The center side is S = length − width − joint; with a {joint} mm joint, e.g. {length} × 100 mm for a 100 × 100 mm center tile.
Frame format for multiple rings: length = 2 × width + joint; with a {joint} mm joint, e.g. exactly {length} × 100 mm.
Center format: square and the same thickness as the frame tile.
Center format: exactly {side} × {side} mm and the same thickness as the frame tile.
Large format: square and the same thickness as the small tile. Large side = 2 × small side + joint; with a {joint} mm joint, for example {side} × {side} mm.
Large format: exactly {side} × {side} mm and the same thickness as the small tile.
Small format: square and the same thickness as the large tile. Small side = (large side − joint) ÷ 2.
Small format: exactly {side} × {side} mm and the same thickness as the large tile.
Stick format for {count} sticks: length > {count} × width + {count} × joint. With a {joint} mm joint, e.g. {length} × 100 mm leaves a 100 × 100 mm insert.
Insert format: square and the same thickness as the parquet sticks. Its side follows from stick length, stick width, count and joint.
Insert format: exactly {side} × {side} mm and the same thickness as the parquet sticks.
Format: regular octagon. Its edge length equals the side of the square insert, for example {side} mm.
Format: regular octagon with an exact edge length of {side} mm and the same thickness as the insert.

material_workspace_laying_herringbone_br: Several parallel tiles form one rectangular branch. The bundle does not have to close as a square, but it must not be wider than the tile is long.
material_workspace_laying_center_stone_r: Ring n uses n frame tiles per side. From 2 rings onward, exactly: length = 2 × width + joint.
material_workspace_laying_basket_stick_c: Two to four parallel sticks form one frame arm. The next bundle is rotated by 90° and the square gap receives its own insert.
material_workspace_laying_strategy_super: The selected tile forms the base module. The preview and room repeat this module seamlessly.
material_workspace_laying_strategy_surfa: The selected tile supplies the format and surface. The layout is regenerated and cut for every real surface.
material_workspace_laying_strategy_adapt: The selected lanes and formats determine whether a repeating SuperTile or a full surface texture is generated.
material_workspace_laying_wild_reference: Fixed editor reference with its origin at the top left. In the room, the layout is regenerated for the real surface, openings and sub-areas.
material_workspace_laying_wild_sequence_: A sufficiently large offcut is placed at either the start or end of the next course. For values above 0, a header piece follows after at most the selected number of full tiles.
material_workspace_laying_wild_installat: These two rules are sufficient: undersized offcuts are discarded and head joints in neighboring courses stay apart.
material_workspace_laying_wild_max_full_: 0 disables header pieces. From 1 onward, the generator inserts the defined header piece after this many full tiles.
material_workspace_laying_wild_head_piec: Used only when the maximum number of full tiles is greater than 0.
material_workspace_laying_wild_always_in: Insert header piece before edge cut
On: a due header piece is always inserted. Off: it is omitted when no further full tile follows.
material_workspace_laying_wild_force_res: 0 disables forced restarts. For x > 0, the course after each group of x starts with a new tile instead of an offcut.
material_workspace_laying_wild_next_cour: Choose whether a suitable offcut from the previous course starts the next course or is placed at its end. With 0 header pieces, only full tiles remain between the course boundaries; required cuts stay at those boundaries.
material_workspace_laying_wild_min_insta: Shorter pieces may not remain after a contour cut either.
material_workspace_laying_wild_min_joint: Smallest horizontal distance between head joints in neighboring courses. 0 disables this spacing rule.
material_workspace_laying_lane_hint: Each lane uses its own main tile and horizontal start offset. All tiles must have the same thickness.

room_workspace_ar_mesh_scan_howto_body:
• Move the device slowly and evenly – no jerky panning.
• Cover every surface: walls, floor, ceiling; circle around corners and niches.
• Watch the colour: green = well captured, red = move closer (now up to ~3.5 m).
• Keep a distance of about 0.3–3.5 m – not too close, not too far.
• For a sharp texture: good lighting, pan slowly, face surfaces head-on.
